title: Etale scalar extension preserves inertia and the invariant square
statement: Let $G$ be a finite group acting by ring automorphisms on a commutative ring $R$. For $H\leq G$ put $R^H=\{r\in R:h(r)=r\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Put $A=R^G$, let $\mathfrak q\subset R$ be prime, and let $I=\{g:g\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q,\ g|_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}=1\}$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak q)$. Let $B$ be an etale $A$-algebra [def-weil-etale-morphism], put $S=B\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and act by $g(b\otimes r)=b\otimes g(r)$. Let $\mathfrak Q\subset S$ be prime with contraction $\mathfrak q$ to $R$. Then its inertia subgroup $\{g:g\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak Q,\ g|_{\operatorname{Frac}(S/\mathfrak Q)}=1\}$ is $I$. The canonical maps $B\longrightarrow S^G$ and $B\otimes_A R^I\longrightarrow S^I$ are isomorphisms of $B$-algebras. Consequently the square with vertices $\operatorname{Spec}S^I,\operatorname{Spec}R^I,\operatorname{Spec}B,\operatorname{Spec}A$ and arrows induced by the canonical ring maps is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], and both horizontal morphisms are etale. Here spectra are as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The point $\mathfrak Q\cap S^I$ maps to $\mathfrak q\cap R^I$. These assertions also apply with $B_b,S_b,\mathfrak Q S_b$ in place of $B,S,\mathfrak Q$ for every $b\in B\setminus(\mathfrak Q\cap B)$. No finiteness of $R$ as an $A$-module or invertibility of $|G|$ is required.

proof.text: For an automorphism $g$ of a ring $T$ and a prime $P$, belonging to inertia is equivalent to $g(t)-t\in P$ for every $t\in T$: this condition gives $g(P)\subseteq P$, and here the finite order of $g$ gives equality; the induced identity on $T/P$ extends to its fraction field. Conversely the inclusion $T/P\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(T/P)$ gives the condition. Thus an inertia element at $\mathfrak Q$ satisfies $1\otimes(g(r)-r)\in\mathfrak Q$ for every $r$, whence $g(r)-r\in\mathfrak q$ by contraction and $g\in I$. Conversely, for $g\in I$ and $s=\sum_j b_j\otimes r_j$, tensor generation gives $g(s)-s=\sum_j(b_j\otimes1)(1\otimes(g(r_j)-r_j))\in\mathfrak Q$. The same criterion now puts $g$ in the inertia at $\mathfrak Q$. This proves equality as subgroups of the given $G$, without any flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0BSS, lemma-inertia-base-change, proof; expanded using the difference criterion on tensor generators

proof.text: By the etale-algebra flatness lemma $B$ is flat over $A$. For $H=G$ and for $H=I$, each $h$ fixes $A=R^G$, so the given action on $R$ is by $A$-algebra automorphisms. Both groups are finite. Apply the flat-invariants comparison with base ring $A$, algebra $D=R$ and scalar algebra $B$. It gives the canonical $B$-algebra isomorphisms $B\otimes_A R^G\simeq S^G$ and $B\otimes_A R^I\simeq S^I$. Since $R^G=A$, the first source is canonically $B$, by $b\otimes a\mapsto ba$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Hence its composite is precisely the asserted map $B\to S^G$.

proof.text: Apply the affine fibre-product formula to the two $A$-algebras $B$ and $R^I$. Its specified projections identify $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A R^I)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}R^I$. The comparison of step 2 sends $b\otimes x$ to the same tensor in $S$. Therefore the maps out of $B$ and $R^I$ are exactly the canonical maps defining the square in the statement. Replacing $B\otimes_A R^I$ by $S^I$ through this isomorphism proves that this square is cartesian.

proof.text: The bottom horizontal map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale by hypothesis. The top horizontal map is its base change along $\operatorname{Spec}R^I\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, by step 3. Stability of etale morphisms under arbitrary base change makes it etale.

proof.text: For $x\in R^I$ the image of $x$ in $S^I$ belongs to $\mathfrak Q\cap S^I$ exactly when $1\otimes x\in\mathfrak Q$, equivalently $x\in\mathfrak q$. Thus the inverse image of $\mathfrak Q\cap S^I$ is $\mathfrak q\cap R^I$, proving the assertion about the point under the induced spectrum map.

proof.text:
Fix $b
otin\mathfrak Q\cap B$. The localization lemma makes $B_b$ etale over $A$. The canonical isomorphism $B_b\otimes_A R\simeq S_b$ sends $(c/b^n)\otimes r$ to $(c\otimes r)/b^n$; its inverse sends $(\sum_j c_j\otimes r_j)/b^n$ to $\sum_j(c_j/b^n)\otimes r_j$. Tensor relations and the fraction relation make these inverse ring maps, and they commute with $G$ because $G$ fixes $b$. The extended ideal $\mathfrak Q S_b$ consists exactly of fractions $s/b^n$ with $s\in\mathfrak Q$: its quotient is $(S/\mathfrak Q)[1/ ar b]$, a nonzero domain since $ ar b
e0$. It is therefore prime and contracts to $\mathfrak Q$, since $b^n s\in\mathfrak Q$ and $b
otin\mathfrak Q$ imply $s\in\mathfrak Q$. In particular its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak q$. Repeat steps 1--5 with $B_b$ and this prime; all their hypotheses have now been verified. They give every localized assertion. Throughout, only finite-group invariants and flatness of the etale algebra were used; neither module-finiteness of $R/A$ nor division by $|G|$ occurred.
